categoryMeta.description: 10K workouts focused on threshold, tempo, stamina, and race-pace durability.

workouts.title: Continuous Threshold Aerobic Intro
workouts.summary: A fundamental introductory session designed to safely introduce continuous threshold running under controlled effort.
workouts.riskReason: Continuous high aerobic output can place stress on the lower leg muscles (calves, shins) if posture slouches under fatigue.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Run continuously at your personal lactate threshold (RPE 6). You should be able to speak short phrases only. Avoid early overcooking.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate stable in high aerobic zone (approx 80-85% max HR).

warmup.name: Aerobic Preparation Jog
warmup.description: 1200m progressive easy jog at conversational effort (RPE 4) to elevate core temperature.

warmup.name: General Mobility Activation
warmup.description: Dynamic flexibility: leg swings, hip circles, followed by 20m high knees and light walking lunges.

mainSet.name: Continuous Threshold Tempo
mainSet.description: Run 25 minutes continuous. Keep the intensity stable; focus on high posture and smooth breathing. Settle in smoothly.

cooldown.name: Flush Walk-Jog
cooldown.description: 800m very easy slow jog and deep breathing walk to promote venous return.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching Session
cooldown.description: 10 mins of static stretching focusing on calves, shins (tibialis), hamstrings, and hip flexors. Do not force range of motion.

easier.description: Reduce tempo duration to 20 minutes continuous.

mainSet.name: Continuous Threshold Tempo (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 20 minutes continuous running at RPE 6.

harder.description: Extend tempo duration to 30 minutes continuous.

mainSet.name: Continuous Threshold Tempo (Extended)
mainSet.description: 30 minutes continuous running at RPE 6.

coachingNotes: Focus on pacing discipline: do not overcook the first 10 minutes. Settle in comfortably.
Practice dynamic calf stretches dynamically before beginning.
Shake out your hands and arms every 5 minutes to stay loose.
commonMistakes: Starting the session too fast, turning it into a 5K race instead of a controlled threshold run.
Holding tension in the shoulders and jaw.
safetyNotes: Continuous pounding on hard pavement increases shin splint risk. Choose flat park trails if possible.
Always stretch calf muscles and Achilles tendons post-run.
Stop immediately if you experience sharp knee or hip pain.

shareCard.purposeText: Build specific lactate clearance threshold and mental stamina.
shareCard.footerNote: Flat road or smooth park paths recommended.

workouts.title: Lactate Threshold Cruise Sets
workouts.summary: A structured threshold interval session utilizing short rest periods to accumulate time at lactate threshold safely.
workouts.riskReason: Continuous high aerobic efforts place steady stress on calves and Achilles; breaking into blocks mitigates early fatigue collapse.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Run each 8-minute block at a controlled threshold effort (RPE 6-7). Settle into a smooth breathing rhythm. Avoid early overcooking.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate stable in high aerobic zone; ensure it drops during the active jog recovery between sets.

warmup.name: Aerobic Preparation Jog
warmup.description: 1200m progressive easy jog at conversational effort (RPE 4) to elevate core temperature.

warmup.name: General Mobility Activation
warmup.description: Dynamic flexibility: leg swings, hip circles, followed by 20m high knees and light walking lunges.

mainSet.name: Lactate Threshold Blocks
mainSet.description: Run 8 minutes at controlled threshold effort, rest 3 minutes with an easy jog, then run a second and third block.

cooldown.name: Flush Walk-Jog
cooldown.description: 800m very easy slow jog and deep breathing walk to promote venous return.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching Session
cooldown.description: 10 mins of static stretching focusing on calves, shins (tibialis), hamstrings, and hip flexors. Do not force range of motion.

easier.description: Reduce block durations to 6 minutes each with 3 minutes easy walking recovery.

mainSet.name: Lactate Threshold Blocks (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 3 × 6 minutes threshold tempo with 180 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase block durations to 10 minutes each to extend the specific training volume.

mainSet.name: Lactate Threshold Blocks (Extended)
mainSet.description: 3 × 10 minutes threshold tempo with 180 seconds jogging recovery.

coachingNotes: Focus on pacing discipline: do not overcook the first block. Keep it smooth.
Use the 3-minute jog recovery to refresh mentally; do not run too fast.
Keep your breathing steady and diaphragmatic.
commonMistakes: Treating the first block as a maximum effort race, forcing a slow or DNF third block.
Skipping the recovery jog and standing still.
safetyNotes: Choose flat trails or soft surfaces to limit calf and shin irritation.
Ensure proper warm up mobilization beforehand.
Stop immediately if sharp shin pain occurs.

shareCard.purposeText: Build specific lactate clearance capability with a mid-session posture reset.
shareCard.footerNote: Flat roads or trails recommended.

workouts.title: Lactate Clearance Over-Under Blocks
workouts.summary: A challenging threshold session alternating sub-threshold and super-threshold efforts within the same repetition to push lactate buffering capabilities.
workouts.riskReason: Repetitive speed adjustments under progressive lactic load expose calves and hamstrings to high mechanical strain.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Run each 1200m repetition alternating: first 800m at threshold pace (RPE 6-7), surge final 400m at 10K race pace (RPE 8). Avoid early overcooking.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate spikes during the 400m surge; recover actively during the 90 seconds walking recovery.

warmup.name: Stamina Priming Jog
warmup.description: 1600m continuous progressive jog, starting very slow and ending with a steady aerobic clip (RPE 4-5) to prepare cardiorespiratory systems.

warmup.name: Dynamic Stamina Drills
warmup.description: Dynamic stretching (10 mins) followed by 2 × 30m A-skips, heel-to-glute cycles, and walking hamstring sweeps.

warmup.name: Rhythmic Pacing Strides
warmup.description: 4 × 60m progressive strides (first two at tempo pace, final two at 10K race pace) to prep neuromuscular patterns.

mainSet.name: Over-Under 1200m Repetitions
mainSet.description: Perform 1200m reps: 800m at controlled threshold pace, accelerate/surge final 400m to 10K race pace. Rest 90 seconds walking between reps.

cooldown.name: Flush Walk-Jog
cooldown.description: 800m very easy slow jog and deep breathing walk to promote venous return.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching Session
cooldown.description: 10 mins of static stretching focusing on calves, shins (tibialis), hamstrings, and hip flexors. Do not force range of motion.

easier.description: Reduce to 3 repetitions with 2 minutes of walking recovery.

mainSet.name: Over-Under 1200m Repetitions (Reduced)
mainSet.description: 3 × 1200m reps (800m threshold / 400m 10K pace) with 120 seconds walking recovery.

harder.description: Increase to 5 repetitions with 90 seconds recovery jog (Strictly for highly conditioned runners).

mainSet.name: Over-Under 1200m Repetitions (Extended)
mainSet.description: 5 × 1200m reps (800m threshold / 400m 10K pace) with 90 seconds recovery jog.

coachingNotes: Focus on pacing discipline: do not overcook the first repetitions. Maintain composure.
This over-under structure trains the body to clear lactate while running fast.
The 400m surge should be a smooth acceleration, not a maximal sprint.
commonMistakes: Sprinting the 400m surge maximal speed, causing early lactic lockout.
Standing still or sitting down during the recovery.
safetyNotes: Thorough dynamic warmup is mandatory. Pay attention to early calf/hamstring soreness.
Ensure spikes are secure if using them on the track curve.
Ensure you perform the legs-up cooldown flushes.

shareCard.purposeText: Build specific lactate buffering and event-finish acceleration capabilities.
shareCard.footerNote: Track or flat marked path required.

workouts.title: Mona Fartlek Adapted 10K
workouts.summary: A continuous fartlek session adapting the legendary 'Mona' structure to build threshold clearance and speed-endurance.
workouts.riskReason: Continuous pace adjustments demand strong eccentric calf control and hamstring flexibility.

intensityGuide.paceGuide: Surge at threshold effort (RPE 7) during hard segments, returning immediately to an easy float jog (RPE 5) during recoveries. No walking. Settle in smoothly and avoid early overcooking.
intensityGuide.hrGuide: Heart rate remains elevated throughout; floats teach the cardiorespiratory system active recovery.

warmup.name: Aerobic Preparation Jog
warmup.description: 1200m progressive easy jog at conversational effort (RPE 4) to elevate core temperature.

warmup.name: General Mobility Activation
warmup.description: Dynamic flexibility: leg swings, hip circles, followed by 20m high knees and light walking lunges.

mainSet.name: Adapted Mona 10K Set
mainSet.description: Perform continuous alternating segments of hard threshold (RPE 7) and easy recovery float jog: 2 × 90s, 4 × 60s, 4 × 30s, 4 × 15s. Settle in and control the early pace. No stopping.

cooldown.name: Flush Walk-Jog
cooldown.description: 800m very easy slow jog and deep breathing walk to promote venous return.

cooldown.name: Static Stretching Session
cooldown.description: 10 mins of static stretching focusing on calves, shins (tibialis), hamstrings, and hip flexors. Do not force range of motion.

easier.description: Omit the 90-second segments, performing: 4 × 60s, 4 × 30s, 4 × 15s with equal duration easy walk recoveries.

mainSet.name: Adapted Mona 10K Set (Reduced)
mainSet.description: Continuous segments: 4 × 60s, 4 × 30s, 4 × 15s. Equal duration easy walk recoveries.

harder.description: Increase the surge segments intensity to target 10K race pace effort (RPE 8) while maintaining the easy float recovery jogs.

mainSet.name: Adapted Mona 10K Set (Race Pace)
mainSet.description: Mona segments at 10K race pace (RPE 8) with easy float recovery jogs: 2 × 90s, 4 × 60s, 4 × 30s, 4 × 15s.

coachingNotes: Focus on pacing discipline: avoid early overcooking. Keep recoveries steady to clear lactate under load.
The secret of Mona Fartlek is the float recovery. Do not jog extremely slow; keep it steady.
This adapted session is excellent to prepare for road race terrain changes.
commonMistakes: Sprinting the 90s segments at 3K/sprint pace, leading to complete recovery collapse and walking.
Walking during the recovery float jogs.
safetyNotes: Fast foot turnover changes demand supple calf muscles and Achilles tendons. Stretch calves thoroughly.
Run on flat, reliable park paths or paved surfaces.
Perform standard cool down stretching.

shareCard.mainSetText: Continuous alternating RPE 7 Surges / Float Recovery Jogs (24-Min)
shareCard.purposeText: Build specific active lactate clearance and neuromuscular pacing play.
shareCard.footerNote: Flat road or park loops recommended.

workouts.title: Advanced Threshold Pacing Ladder

intensityGuide.hrGuide: Maintain a steady, controlled heart rate in high aerobic zones (approx 80-85% max HR).

warmup.name: Rhythmic Pacing Strides

mainSet.name: Lactate Cruise Pacing Ladder
mainSet.description: Run progressive reps at threshold effort: 1200m, 1600m, 2000m, 1200m. Rest exactly 120 seconds easy recovery jog between reps. Settle in safely.

cooldown.name: Extended Active Flush Jog
cooldown.description: 1200m very slow, relaxed recovery jog on turf or grass to promote circulation and passive lactic clearance.

easier.description: Omit the 2000m rep, performing: 1200m, 1600m, 1200m with 150 seconds recovery jog.

mainSet.name: Lactate Cruise Pacing Ladder (Reduced)
mainSet.description: Threshold reps: 1200m, 1600m, 1200m. 150 seconds recovery jog.

harder.description: Decrease recovery jog duration to 90 seconds to push lactate buffering capabilities.

mainSet.name: Lactate Cruise Pacing Ladder (Extended)
mainSet.description: Threshold reps: 1200m, 1600m, 2000m, 1200m with 90 seconds recovery jog.

coachingNotes: Focus on pacing discipline: do not overcook the early segments. Keep the 2000m block steady.
Pacing control is vital on the 2000m rep; settle into a smooth, relaxed rhythm early.
Keep recovery jogs structured; do not walk or stop completely to encourage active clearance.
commonMistakes: Sprinting the initial 1200m at 5K race pace, leading to muscle lockup and failing the rest of the ladder.
Standing still during recovery jogs.
safetyNotes: High cumulative volume requires thorough dynamic warmups.
Calves and Achilles tendons are loaded extensively; wear supportive shoes.
Perform the extended legs-up cooldown flushes.
